scams.name: Ayutthaya Train Station ‘Mafia’ Tuk-Tuk Intercept
scams.description: You arrive by train at Ayutthaya Railway Station after the 20-baht local ride from Bangkok Hua Lamphong. Outside the station, a fleet of *tuk-tuks* waits. A driver quotes 800 baht per person for a ‘full-day temple tour’ — a number you can’t verify because you don’t know Ayutthaya geography yet. r/ThailandTourism ‘Did I just almost got scammed or something?’ captures the arrival intimidation: ‘Lots of mafia tuk-tuks waiting outside. I had ordered a taxi on InDrive…’ The fair rate for tuk-tuk hire in Ayutthaya (driver plus vehicle, four to six hours visiting five temples) is 200–300 baht per hour — so 800–1,200 baht total for half a day for the whole group, not per person.
scams.avoidance: Buy the 20-baht SRT 3rd-class ticket at the official Hua Lamphong counter and ignore anyone in a ‘uniform’ outside. At Ayutthaya station, walk past the tuk-tuk fleet and open Grab or inDrive. Hire a tuk-tuk or *songthaew* at 200–300 baht per hour for the whole vehicle (not per person) for temple-hopping. Or rent a bicycle at 50 baht a day; the ruins are within a 5 km loop and cycling is the local standard. Refuse any tour that includes a stop at a ‘jewelry shop’ or ‘silk store’ — these are commission detours, not sightseeing.
scams.location: Ayutthaya Railway Station entrance, Bangkok Hua Lamphong departure platforms

scams.name: Fake ‘Tourist Information Centre’ Package Sale
scams.description: A polite person in a branded shirt approaches you near Hua Lamphong station: ‘Tourist Information? I can help you plan Ayutthaya!’ They walk you fifty meters to a storefront marked ‘Tourism Authority of Thailand’ or similar. Inside, a ‘consultant’ at a desk covered in maps and brochures sells you a 3,500-baht Ayutthaya day package that would cost 200 baht if you just took the local train and a tuk-tuk. r/ThailandTourism ‘Thailand Scam — what would be wise of me to do’ documents the pattern: ‘I got scammed into jumping on a tuk-tuk seeing temples and planning a trip around Thailand through a tourist information centre.’ The storefront is unaffiliated with the real TAT, and the package routes you through commission shops.
scams.avoidance: The real Tourism Authority of Thailand is at 1600 New Phetchaburi Road in Bangkok and 108 Moo 3 Pratuchai in Ayutthaya — not a Khao San storefront. Never follow a ‘tourist info’ recruiter to a shop; real TIC staff don’t work the street. Book Ayutthaya as DIY: a 20-baht SRT train, a 200 baht-per-hour tuk-tuk at destination, and either free entry or 50-baht temple admission. For packaged day tours, use Klook, Viator, or GetYourGuide with verified operators. Pay by credit card for dispute leverage if the booking goes bad.
scams.location: Bangkok around Hua Lamphong + Khao San Road, Ayutthaya station vicinity

scams.name: Ayutthaya Elephant Ride Overcharge & Ethics
scams.description: Outside the Wat Phra Si Sanphet ruins, a *mahout* in traditional dress offers an ‘elephant ride around the ruins’ for 400 baht. You agree. After 20 minutes the handler stops and says you owe another 600 baht for the ‘extended route’ you didn’t request. r/ThailandTourism captures the pattern: the first price is always half the real charge — once you are committed and the elephant has walked fifteen minutes, the handler can add ‘time extension’ or ‘extra route’ fees that feel impossible to refuse mid-saddle.
scams.avoidance: Don’t ride elephants in Ayutthaya. Every ethical travel guide warns against it, and the welfare conditions at the ride camps fail basic welfare standards. For an ethical elephant experience, visit Elephant Nature Park (Chiang Mai) or BEES Sanctuary — never a ride-based camp. Rent a bicycle at 50 baht a day (shops throughout the historic park) to visit the ruins. Budget for admission: 50 baht per site, or 220 baht for the combined pass. If a handler approaches, decline and walk on — no elephant interaction is needed to enjoy Ayutthaya.
scams.location: Ayutthaya Elephant Palace & Royal Kraal, various ruin-area elephant camps

scams.name: Floating Market Day-Trip Van Bait-and-Switch
scams.description: You book an ‘Ayutthaya + Floating Market Combo’ day trip from a Khao San booth for 1,500 baht. The promised itinerary: morning floating market (Damnoen Saduak), afternoon Ayutthaya. The reality: the van picks you up 40 minutes late and stops at an orchid farm (commission), a cobra farm (commission), and a silk shop (commission). You reach Damnoen Saduak at 10:30am — the market is already winding down (legitimate hours 6–9am). You get 40 minutes at the ‘floating market,’ which is a tourist sample version two streets from the real one. Ayutthaya is a two-hour stop at only two temples. r/ThailandTourism ‘Floating Market Van Scam? I’m worried.’ documents the exact pattern.
scams.avoidance: Don’t combo Ayutthaya with a floating market. Give Ayutthaya a dedicated day. For floating markets, visit Amphawa on weekend evenings (local, authentic) or arrive at Damnoen Saduak by 7am via Grab. For Ayutthaya, take the 20-baht SRT 3rd-class train plus a 200 baht-per-hour tuk-tuk at destination. Book any day tour via Klook, Viator, or GetYourGuide — never from a Khao San storefront. Confirm each temple and site by name on the written itinerary before you pay.
scams.location: Bangkok-based day trips to Damnoen Saduak, Amphawa + Ayutthaya combo tours

scams.name: Temple ‘Closed’ Detour to Commission Shop
scams.description: You arrive at Wat Mahathat — home of the famous Buddha head entwined in tree roots — and a man near the entrance tells you it’s closed for restoration this morning, but he can take you to another beautiful temple ten minutes away. That temple is real. The detour ends with a mandatory thirty minutes at an ‘authentic Thai silk weaving center’ where you are pressured to buy. This is the Grand Palace ‘closed today’ script, ported to Ayutthaya. r/ThailandTourism ‘Your 1st Negative Experience in Thailand’ confirms it runs the same way here.
scams.avoidance: Verify temple hours on ayutthaya-history.com or Google Maps before you arrive; the major ruins are almost never closed mid-day. Ignore anyone at a temple entrance who offers to ‘guide’ you elsewhere — walk past them and enter yourself. Pay admission (50 baht per site, 220 baht for the combined pass) at the official kiosk inside the gate. A tuk-tuk waiting at an entrance is a commission tour; skip it and flag a circulating one. Refuse any ‘side stop’ for shopping as part of a temple tour — that is the entire revenue model.
scams.location: Wat Mahathat entrance, Wat Phra Si Sanphet, Wat Chaiwatthanaram access paths
